---
title: Publishing a template
description: Add a directory to cubeshipd/cubeship-templates through a pull request.
---

Templates live in [cubeshipd/cubeship-templates](https://github.com/cubeshipd/cubeship-templates). Open a pull request that adds or changes one directory named with the template slug, such as `umami` or `uptime-kuma`.

Each directory needs three files:

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `template.yaml` | The resources and inputs. Set top-level `name` to the display name. At most 256 KB. |
| `README.md` | What the template installs and what to do after installing. At most 512 KB. |
| `icon.png` | A square PNG, 128 to 1024 pixels per side, at most 512 KB. |

For a source-built app, keep its Dockerfile and any files it copies inside the same directory. Set `repo: https://github.com/cubeshipd/cubeship-templates` and `ref: main:<directory>`. The installer pins the build to the cataloged commit and uses that directory as the build context.

The directory name identifies the template in URLs. `name` controls how it appears in the catalog; changing it does not change the URL. Add this line to the YAML for editor checks:

```yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://cubeship.dev/schema/template/v1.json
```

CI validates every directory with Cubeship's validator. The catalog reads the current `main` commit about every five minutes and publishes all directories together. If any directory is invalid, it keeps the previous valid snapshot and logs the error until it is corrected. Relative links and images in a README resolve within that directory at the cataloged commit.

There are no template releases or updates to existing installations. `version: 1` in the YAML identifies the file format. Image tags and source refs inside apps still describe what a **new install** will run. To change an existing installation, change its apps on that Cubeship instance.
